1.explanation:
• Toggle/Toggle.mdx is the Storybook page that shows the live examples and the prop-table for aria-labelledby and hideLabel. It’s the first place consumers look for guidance on those props.  
• Toggle/docs/overview.mdx gives the longer-form usage details and examples for Toggle; this is where we’d explain best practices around hideLabel and aria-labelledby (or propose removing the requirement).  
• FormLabel/FormLabel.mdx and FormLabel/docs/overview.mdx describe the underlying labeling API (for=, id=, accessible naming)—since the proposed workaround uses a separate <label> element, it’s useful to cross-reference how FormLabel handles for/id pairing and how that interacts with Toggle internally.
1.bug_scenario:
From the screenshots you can see that passing hideLabel={true} on the <Toggle> does not actually remove the rendered label. Instead it moves the labelText to the side. Only when you also supply aria-labelledby and point it at an external <label> does the visual label disappear (and accessibility text remains).</br></br>1. First two side-by-side images show hideLabel={true} vs hideLabel={false}: neither truly hides the label, they only reposition it (side vs. top).  
2. The prop-table screenshot shows that neither the aria-labelledby nor hideLabel entries call out this interdependency.  
3. A subsequent screenshot illustrates the pattern of adding your own <label for="toggle-1">newLabel</label> plus aria-labelledby=“otherLabel” on the Toggle to finally get a hidden label.</br></br>This confusion prompted the bug: the storybook docs for Toggle need better guidance on hideLabel’s behavior (and perhaps the requirement for aria-labelledby), or the component itself may be simplified to respect hideLabel without that extra prop.
